q: A Pune bakery owner hires a freelancer for Instagram captions. According to the course, what is she really paying for?
options: Access to the AI tools the freelancer subscribes to
The number of hours the freelancer spends writing
Outcomes: timely, on-brand posts that bring people into the shop
Captions that are proven to be written without AI
explain: Clients do not pay for AI; they pay for outcomes, and AI is simply a tool you use to deliver them.

q: Which introduction best shows a clear niche?
options: I am a freelancer offering writing, social media, Excel and slides
I write monthly blogs and LinkedIn posts for CA firms so partners save their weekends
I am a passionate, detail-oriented content creator open to any project
I use the latest AI tools to deliver any content you need, fast
explain: A niche combines a specific client type with a specific problem, making you memorable and easy to refer.

q: Why should an offer like 'Instagram Starter Month' include a 'what's not included' line?
options: It makes the package look bigger than competitors' offers
Platforms such as Fiverr require it on every listing
It lets you charge a higher price for the core package
It prevents scope creep, a common cause of freelancer stress
explain: Listing exclusions such as paid ads or reels shooting stops a project from quietly growing beyond what was agreed.

q: You ask AI for captions for hand-painted tea cups but forget to say they are microwave-unsafe. What is the main risk?
options: The AI may invent product facts, such as claiming they are dishwasher safe
The captions will be too short to post on Instagram
The AI will refuse to write about handmade products
The captions will be in the wrong language for the audience
explain: If you leave out real facts, AI may make them up, so always give it accurate product details.

q: Ravi is building a spec sample for a fictional grocery store. What should his case study say under 'Result'?
options: An estimated engagement increase, such as 40 percent
A short testimonial written in a friend's name
What the client would receive and why the work should be effective
The logo of a real grocery chain to add credibility
explain: For spec work, never invent metrics or testimonials; explain your reasoning and label it clearly as a sample.

q: Why does hourly pricing become less attractive once AI helps you work faster?
options: Clients refuse to pay hourly rates for AI-assisted work
If you finish faster, you earn less for the same deliverable
Hourly pricing cannot include revisions or communication
Freelance platforms no longer allow hourly contracts
explain: Project pricing lets you benefit from your own efficiency, while hourly pricing pays you less as you speed up.

q: A local client says your social media package is too expensive. What does the course recommend?
options: Offer a smaller scope at a lower price with the same quality
Cut the price by half to win the first project
Keep the same scope and quietly skip the quality checks
Refuse to negotiate and end the conversation
explain: Adjusting scope rather than dropping your rate protects your pricing while still helping the client.

q: Neha is new to freelancing and wants her first one or two clients. Where does the course suggest she start?
options: Cold proposals on international marketplaces only
Bulk WhatsApp messages to local business numbers
Paid ads targeting businesses across India
Her warm and lukewarm networks, where trust already exists
explain: First clients often come from people who know you or are one step away, because trust already exists.

q: Which opening line makes an Upwork proposal most likely to be read?
options: Dear Sir/Madam, I am a hardworking freelancer with excellent skills
I hope this message finds you well and that you are doing great
You mentioned duplicates from three sources and mixed phone formats; I have cleaned similar lists
I have years of experience in many different fields and tools
explain: A strong hook mirrors a specific detail from the brief, showing the client you actually read it.

q: You sent a respectful cold message to a café owner and got no reply. What should you do next?
options: Message them daily until they respond
Follow up once or twice with added value, then stop gracefully
Ask a friend to message them from another number
Assume the answer is no and never follow up at all
explain: Many replies come after a follow-up, but you should follow up at most twice and then respect silence.

q: After a kickoff call with a boutique owner, what should you send before starting work?
options: A written summary of deliverables, dates, revisions and approvers, asking her to confirm
The first finished batch of posts so she can see your style
An invoice for the full project amount
A general thank-you note with no specific details
explain: Confirming scope, timelines and approvers in writing protects both sides and prevents confusion later.

q: In a simple service agreement, when does ownership of the final deliverables commonly pass to the client?
options: As soon as the first draft is shared
When the contract is signed, before any work begins
Once full payment is received
Never; the freelancer always keeps ownership
explain: A common approach is that the client owns the final deliverables on full payment, while you keep your general templates and know-how.

q: A new international client pays more than your invoice and asks you to refund the difference. What is this most likely to be?
options: A generous tip for fast delivery
A normal currency conversion adjustment
An advance for the next project
An overpayment scam where the original payment is later reversed
explain: In overpayment scams the original payment often turns out to be fraudulent and gets reversed after you refund.

q: Ritu is comparing ways to receive payments from a US client. What should she compare first?
options: Which service has the best-known brand name
The final rupee amount she receives after fees and conversion
Which service her friends use most often
Only the headline transfer fee shown on the website
explain: Fees, conversion margins and bank charges all reduce what you receive, so compare the final rupee amount.

q: A tiffin service uses AI to draft WhatsApp quick replies. Which instruction best prevents wrong answers?
options: Use only the facts I give; write [CHECK] where something is missing
Make the replies sound as friendly as possible
Include typical delivery charges and refund rules
Keep every reply under ten words
explain: The [CHECK] instruction stops the AI inventing details like a delivery charge or refund policy you do not have.

q: For monthly bookkeeping, what is the safest way to get totals by category from your transactions sheet?
options: Paste the full bank statement into AI and ask for the totals
Estimate totals by eye and adjust at year end
Ask AI to write spreadsheet formulas, then test them on rows you know
Let AI file the GST return directly from the statement
explain: Spreadsheet formulas are reliable and reusable, while AI arithmetic on pasted data can be wrong.

q: Anil keeps forgetting steps when delivering his social media package. What does the course suggest building?
options: A longer contract with stricter penalty clauses
A bigger set of AI tools to automate every step
A higher price so he can afford more time per project
A delivery SOP with numbered steps, prompts, checklists and common problems
explain: An SOP turns experience into a repeatable process that catches mistakes and keeps quality consistent.

q: A bakery client asks what results your social media package will deliver. Which promise is appropriate?
options: 12 high-quality posts on schedule, with honest notes that results depend on many factors
Double your sales within 30 days or your money back
Guaranteed 10,000 new followers by the end of the month
Your bakery will rank first on Google for cakes in your city
explain: Promise what you control, such as quality, quantity and timeliness, and be honest that outcomes depend on many factors.
